title: BDS Case Files
description: Cooperative workplace mysteries • 2–10 players • 5 specialist roles • 6 team actions • Objective: identify the suspect, motive, and method

title: Keep it fictional
description: Acknowledge the fictional-entertainment notice before entering • Use a made-up detective alias, not personal information • All characters, clues, rumors, and outcomes are fictional • Playful workplace mix-ups—not real incidents or allegations • Active room state stays in memory; no database or case history

title: Create a room. Assemble your team.
description: Host chooses Start New Case and shares the room code • Teammates choose Join Case and enter the code • Rooms support 2–10 players • Specialist roles are assigned randomly; larger teams may repeat roles • New players join before the host starts the investigation

title: Read the case briefing
description: Review the case title, summary, and location • Meet six fictional suspects and compare their profiles and alibis • Start with two evidence items and the case timeline • Read 2–4 playful rumors when enabled • Treat rumors as leads—not proof

title: Use your specialist advantage
description: Forensics Expert: one extra private evidence clue • Interviewer: one free follow-up question during the investigation • Archivist: a private historical background clue • Analyst: a private timeline hint • Profiler: a private motive hint

title: Ten actions. Six team uses.
description: Interview Suspect • Review Emails • Examine Scene • Review Security Logs • Check Timeline • Verify Alibi • Search Office • Analyze Evidence • Review Project Tracker • Audit Recent Changes

title: Vote on the next investigation
description: Each connected player votes for one available action • A strict majority completes the action immediately • If everyone votes without a majority, the largest vote total wins • A tie favors the host’s vote among tied leaders; otherwise fixed action order decides • Each completed action spends one team use and clears the votes • Completed actions cannot be repeated

title: Compare clues—not just guesses
description: New clues appear on the shared evidence board • Compare helpful clues, contradictions, red herrings, and timeline details • Share your private specialist information in team chat when enabled • Use suspect profiles and alibis to check your theory • Keep personal investigation notes private; notes clear on reload or case replacement

title: Make one final accusation
description: Discuss the evidence and agree on a theory • Only the host submits the final accusation • Choose one suspect, one motive, and one method • Review the choices before confirming: one filing, no appeals • The reveal shows the solution, clue explanations, team score, and rank

title: Accuracy earns points. Unused actions add a bonus.
description: Correct suspect: +50 points • Correct motive: +25 points • Correct method: +25 points • Each unused team action: +10 points • Example: all three correct + three unused actions = 130 points

title: Earn your team rank
description: Rookie Detectives: below 50 points • Junior Investigators: 50–74 points • Senior Investigators: 75–99 points • Elite Detectives: 100–129 points • Master Detectives: 130+ points • Balance confident deduction against the value of unused actions

title: Host controls and replay
description: Disable rumors to hide playful leads • Disable chat to stop discussion and discard existing messages • Reset Case clears the case and returns the same team to the lobby • Start New Case replaces the case while keeping the room, team, and settings • Both actions discard previous evidence, chat, notes, votes, and results • Repeat: Brief → Discuss → Vote → Investigate → Accuse → Reveal
